A position detection device is configured to detect a position of the electric drive dump truck; a vehicle speed detection device is configured to detect a vehicle speed of the electric drive dump truck; and a storage section is configured to store a position of the trolley lines and a time period, hereinafter referred to as a moving-up time, from when the power collection units start moving upward until the power collection units contact the trolley lines. outputs.L2: An electric-drive dump truck operates by bringing power collection units into contact with trolley lines to receive electrical power. These power collection units are raised and lowered by lifting devices. The truck includes a position detection device that determines the truck’s location, a vehicle speed detection device that measures its speed, and a storage section that stores both the location of the trolley lines and the time required for the power collection units to reach and contact the trolley lines after they begin rising, referred to as the “moving-up time.” A control device generates a signal indicating that the power collection units may be raised, based on the truck’s detected position and speed, the stored trolley line position, and the moving-up time.
outputs.L3:
An electric drive dump truck is configured to receive electrical power from external trolley lines while traveling. To obtain this power, the dump truck is equipped with movable power collection units that can be brought into contact with the trolley lines.

The power collection units are raised and lowered by lifting devices. When the dump truck approaches a section of road where trolley lines are installed, the lifting devices move the power collection units upward so that they can contact the trolley lines. When contact is no longer required, the lifting devices can move the power collection units downward.

The dump truck also includes a position detection device and a vehicle speed detection device. The position detection device detects the current location of the dump truck, while the vehicle speed detection device detects the traveling speed of the dump truck.

In addition, a storage section stores information relating to the position of the trolley lines. The storage section also stores a moving-up time, which is the amount of time required for the power collection units to move upward and make contact with the trolley lines.

A control device uses the detected position of the dump truck, the detected vehicle speed, the stored trolley line position, and the stored moving-up time to determine an appropriate timing for raising the power collection units. Based on this determination, the control device decides when the power collection units can be moved upward so that they contact the trolley lines at the proper time while the dump truck is traveling.
outputs.L4:
An electric drive dump truck is equipped with power collection units that can be raised and lowered in order to receive electric power from overhead trolley lines while the truck is traveling. To ensure that these power collection units make contact with the trolley lines at the appropriate moment, the truck includes a control system that determines the proper timing for raising the units.

The control system detects the current position and traveling speed of the dump truck. It also stores, in advance, information indicating the locations of trolley lines along the travel route. Using this information, the system determines the distance between the truck’s current position and an upcoming trolley-line section. In addition, the system takes into account the time required for the power collection units to move from their lowered position to a raised position where they can contact the overhead trolley lines.

Based on the truck speed, the distance to the trolley line, and the raising time of the power collection units, the control system calculates when the lifting operation should begin. If the units are raised too early, they may remain unnecessarily elevated before reaching the trolley line, which can increase the risk of interference or damage. If they are raised too late, they may fail to contact the trolley line at the beginning of the trolley-powered section, resulting in unreliable power pickup. By starting the raising operation at the calculated timing, the system enables the power collection units to reach the proper contact position just as the truck arrives beneath the trolley lines.

This control improves the reliability of power collection during truck operation. It allows the dump truck to transition smoothly from battery or engine-generated electric drive to trolley-line power, reducing missed contact events and helping maintain stable vehicle operation. As a result, the dump truck can more effectively use external electric power while traveling along trolley-equipped routes, improving operational efficiency and reducing the burden on onboard power sources.
outputs.L5:
An electric drive is a system that uses electrical energy to create motion. It usually consists of an electric motor, a power converter, a controller, and a mechanical load. Electric drives are widely used in modern industry, transportation, and household appliances because they are efficient, reliable, and easy to control.

The main part of an electric drive is the electric motor. It converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. Depending on the application, the motor may be a direct current motor, an induction motor, or a synchronous motor. The controller regulates the speed, torque, and direction of rotation, allowing the drive to work accurately and safely.

Electric drives are used in many areas. In factories, they operate pumps, fans, conveyors, and machine tools. In transportation, they power electric cars, trains, and elevators. They are also found in washing machines, air conditioners, and computer cooling systems.

One of the biggest advantages of an electric drive is its high efficiency. It can reduce energy consumption and lower operating costs. Electric drives also produce less noise and pollution compared with many mechanical or fuel-based systems. Because of these benefits, electric drives play an important role in modern technology and sustainable development.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an electric drive dump truck that raises trolley power collectors based on vehicle position, speed, stored trolley line location, and the time required for the collectors to reach the trolley wires.
counterfactuals.output: An electric drive dump truck includes an onboard electric propulsion system and one or more movable trolley power collectors configured to selectively engage overhead trolley wires. A positioning system determines a current position of the dump truck, and a controller stores or accesses map data identifying a location of a trolley line. The controller determines, based on the current position, vehicle speed, the stored trolley line location, and a deployment time required for the trolley power collectors to move from a stowed position to an engagement position, a deployment initiation point or time at which raising of the trolley power collectors should begin. In response, the controller commands actuation of the trolley power collectors before the dump truck reaches the trolley line so that the collectors arrive at or near the engagement position when the vehicle reaches the overhead trolley wires, thereby enabling automatic or semi-automatic connection to trolley power while reducing missed engagements, operator workload, and unnecessary collector deployment.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention in formal patent language involving a trolley-assisted mining dump truck with liftable power collection units, position and speed sensors, memory storing trolley line positions and moving-up time, and a controller that determines when the collectors may be raised.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention is disclosed relating to a trolley-assisted mining dump truck configured to travel along a haul road provided with an overhead trolley line.

The mining dump truck comprises a vehicle body, an electric drive system, and at least one liftable power collection unit configured to be selectively moved between a lowered, non-contact position and a raised, power-collecting position for receiving electric power from the overhead trolley line. The power collection unit may include a pantograph, trolley pole, current collector, or other collector assembly adapted to contact the trolley line when raised.

The dump truck further comprises a position sensor configured to detect or estimate a current position of the dump truck, and a speed sensor configured to detect or estimate a current traveling speed of the dump truck. A memory is provided for storing trolley-line positional information representative of positions of one or more trolley-line sections along the haul road. The memory further stores moving-up time information representative of a time required for the power collection unit to move from the lowered position to the raised position.

A controller is operatively connected to the power collection unit, the position sensor, the speed sensor, and the memory. The controller is configured to determine, based on the current position of the dump truck, the current traveling speed of the dump truck, the stored trolley-line positional information, and the stored moving-up time information, whether raising of the power collection unit is permitted. In particular, the controller may calculate a predicted position of the dump truck at a time when the power collection unit will reach the raised position, and may permit raising of the power collection unit when the predicted position corresponds to a position beneath a trolley-line section suitable for power collection.

In one embodiment, the controller inhibits raising of the power collection unit when the predicted position is outside a predetermined permissible region associated with the trolley line, thereby preventing the collector from being raised before the dump truck reaches the trolley line or after the dump truck has passed beyond a suitable trolley-line section. The controller may issue a raise command only when the dump truck is located at a position upstream of the trolley line by a distance corresponding to the current speed multiplied by the moving-up time, optionally with an additional safety margin.

Accordingly, the invention enables reliable and automatic timing of the raising of liftable power collection units on a trolley-assisted mining dump truck, reducing the likelihood of misalignment with the overhead trolley line and improving safe transition from non-trolley operation to trolley-powered operation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a single-paragraph technical summary of a control system for an electric dump truck that contacts overhead trolley lines, using detected truck position and speed plus stored trolley-line position and collector lift time to output a permission signal for raising the collectors.
counterfactuals.output: The control system for an electric dump truck determines when to permit raising its current collectors to contact overhead trolley lines by combining real-time vehicle data with stored infrastructure data. It detects the truck’s current position and traveling speed, references stored positional information for the trolley-line section ahead, and accounts for the known time required for the collectors to lift from their stowed position to the contact position. Based on these inputs, the controller predicts whether the collectors will reach the overhead lines at an appropriate location and timing, and outputs a permission signal only when raising the collectors can be performed safely and reliably while the truck is approaching or entering the trolley-line zone.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent claim-like description for a trolley line power collection control device on an electric drive dump truck, including lifting devices, position detection, vehicle speed detection, storage of trolley positions and moving-up time, and control logic for move-up authorization.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A trolley line power collection control device for an electric drive dump truck**, the electric drive dump truck being configured to travel using electric power collected from an overhead trolley line by a power collector, the control device comprising:

   - a **lifting device** configured to raise and lower the power collector relative to the vehicle so as to move the power collector between a lowered position and a trolley-line contact position;

   - a **position detection device** configured to detect a current position of the electric drive dump truck;

   - a **vehicle speed detection device** configured to detect a travelling speed of the electric drive dump truck;

   - a **storage unit** configured to store:
     - trolley position information indicating positions at which the overhead trolley line is installed, and
     - moving-up time information indicating a time required for the power collector to move upward from the lowered position to a position capable of contacting the trolley line; and

   - a **control unit** configured to determine whether to authorize upward movement of the power collector by the lifting device based on:
     - the current position detected by the position detection device,
     - the travelling speed detected by the vehicle speed detection device,
     - the trolley position information stored in the storage unit, and
     - the moving-up time information stored in the storage unit.

2. **The trolley line power collection control device according to claim 1**, wherein the control unit calculates a predicted position of the electric drive dump truck after elapse of the moving-up time based on the current position and the travelling speed, and authorizes upward movement of the power collector when the predicted position corresponds to a position at which the trolley line is present.

3. **The trolley line power collection control device according to claim 1**, wherein the control unit prohibits upward movement of the power collector when the electric drive dump truck is determined not to reach a trolley-line installation position within the moving-up time.

4. **The trolley line power collection control device according to claim 1**, wherein the storage unit stores, as the trolley position information, at least one of a start position of a trolley section, an end position of the trolley section, and route information defining a travel path along which the trolley line is installed.

5. **The trolley line power collection control device according to claim 1**, wherein the lifting device is controlled to start raising the power collector before the electric drive dump truck reaches a trolley-line start position, such that the power collector reaches the trolley-line contact position at or near the trolley-line start position.

6. **The trolley line power collection control device according to claim 1**, wherein the control unit determines a move-up authorization timing based on a distance from the current position to a trolley-line start position and a travel distance of the electric drive dump truck during the moving-up time.

7. **The trolley line power collection control device according to claim 1**, wherein the control unit outputs a move-up authorization signal to the lifting device only when the travelling speed is within a predetermined range suitable for power collection from the trolley line.

8. **The trolley line power collection control device according to claim 1**, wherein the position detection device comprises at least one of a satellite positioning receiver, a map matching unit, a travel distance sensor, an inertial sensor, or a route position calculation unit.

9. **The trolley line power collection control device according to claim 1**, wherein the vehicle speed detection device comprises at least one of a wheel speed sensor, a motor speed sensor, a vehicle controller, or a travel distance calculation unit.

10. **The trolley line power collection control device according to claim 1**, wherein the control unit is configured to prevent erroneous raising of the power collector at a position where no trolley line is present, thereby reducing risk of contact between the power collector and surrounding structures.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the disclosed electric drive dump truck system: movable power collection units receive power from trolley lines, sensors detect position and speed, storage holds trolley line locations and collector raising time, and a controller signals when the collectors can move up.
counterfactuals.output: The system is an electric-drive dump truck equipped to use overhead trolley lines for power. It has movable power collection units that can be raised to contact the trolley lines and lowered when not in use. Sensors detect the truck’s current position and speed, while onboard storage contains information such as the known locations of trolley lines and the time required to raise the collectors. A controller uses the truck’s position, speed, trolley-line location data, and collector-raising time to determine whether the collectors can be moved up in time to safely contact the trolley lines, and then outputs a signal indicating when raising is permitted.
